messages:
alex: seeing a small spike of Xid 13 and 31 on rack-r7b-usw2 overnight, started ~3387654200. tenant affinity looks suspicious — same tenant hitting embedder-heavy small-batch workload :thinking_face:
maria: can you paste the top errors? stack traces or dmesg?
alex: throwing logs, trimmed:
````
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 13, pid=4321 Ch 00000000 00000000
[ 1234.568000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, pid=4321 Ch 00000000 00000000
[ 1234.568100] pcieport 0000:3c:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id 00e8
````
jordan: thanks. looks like PCIe corrected errors + Xid 13/31. common pattern when a card is flaky under certain small-batch workloads (high decode concurrency).
maria: what's ECC count on that card? low ECC but increasing correctable errors might indicate link flapping. nvidia-smi snippet?
alex: `nvidia-smi -q -i 3`
````
GPU 03: ECC Errors (Volatile): 0
GPU 03: ECC Errors (Aggregate): 12
GPU 03: Retired Pages: 0
````
lee: aggregate 12 correctables over last 24h is notable. also PCIe AER above. could be cable / riser causing intermittent resets.
ops-bot: detected 6% latency spike on embedder route around same time window. tagging @eng-sre and @hw-support.
maria: any recent changes? kernel, firmware, or batchshape changes?
alex: no kernel/firmware. product changed default embedder batchshape to small micro-batches (1-4) and added more parallel streams 2 days ago.
jordan: hypothesis: smaller micro-batches increase scheduler churn and push higher concurrency through the same card, exposing marginal PCIe link. can we repro with an A/B test?
lee: suggest soft-drain the affected card, move tenants off, run burn-in with `--opencl-regen` style stress for 6h. if errors persist, replace card.
drain-bot: initiated soft-drain on node rack-r7b-usw2-03. moving tasks now, ETA 12m.
maria: also collect full `dmesg -T`, `lspci -vvv` and NV driver logs. I'll run telemetry correlation to see if other racks show same tenant pattern.
jordan: I'll run a quick cohort query: group by tenant, op_type, batch_shape, and GPU model; correlate with Xid tags. will post results in 20m.
lee: if cohort shows single-tenant concentration we should consider tenant isolation or throttling until HW verified. also log a cost note — tenant causing repeated HW churn increases baseline replacement costs.
alex: agreed. action items:
- jordan: run cohort join and post CSV (due +20m)
- maria: gather logs and file HW ticket with vendor if we see PCIe corrected errors persist (due +2h)
- lee: coordinate soft-replace plan if errors > 5/hour after burn-in (due +6h)
- ops-bot: keep routing fallback to other capacity until node healthy
jordan: posted preliminary table: tenant T-74 accounts for 78% of Xid events on that node, op_type=embedder, batch_shape=(1-4), concurrency high.
maria: okay that's pretty conclusive. leaning towards noisy tenant causing marginal hardware to fail faster. recommend temporary tenant rate limit and hardware check.
lee: I'll open a quick remediation PR to add a soft throttle on embedder default concurrency and tag it for rollout tomorrow morning.
alex: thanks all. will monitor post-drain and update thread. :thumbsup:
